title: Search Project-Wide
summary: Chapter 18 explains how to search across an entire project from within Vim. It presents :grep as a wrapper for external grep-like programs, shows how grepprg and grepformat control the command and parse its output (including ack with --nogroup and --column), and introduces :vimgrep for searching multiple files with Vim's own regex engine. It also covers quickfix navigation, file and argument-list patterns such as ##, and reusing the current search pattern or search history.

commands.evidence: Behind the scenes, Vim executes grep -n Waldo * in the shell for us. Rather than printing grep’s output, Vim does something much more useful. It parses the results and builds a quickfix list from them. We can navigate through the results using the :cnext/:cprev commands and all of the other techniques that we explored in Chapter 17, Compile Code and Navigate Errors

concepts.name: :grep external wrapper
concepts.evidence: Vim’s :grep command acts as a wrapper to an external grep (or grep-like) program. Using this wrapper, we can have grep search for a pattern across multiple files without leaving Vim, and then we can navigate the results using the quickfix list.

concepts.name: quickfix list
concepts.evidence: The :vimgrep command populates the quickfix list with one entry for each line that contains a match.

concepts.name: grepprg setting
concepts.evidence: The ‘grepprg’ setting specifies what to run in the shell when Vim’s :grep command is executed ('grepprg'ⓘ). The ‘grepformat’ setting tells Vim how to parse the output returned by the :grep command (see 'grepformat'ⓘ). On Unix systems, the defaults are these:

concepts.name: errorformat-style match tokens
concepts.evidence: For each record, %f matches the filename (department-store.txt or goldrush.txt), %l matches the line number, and %m matches the text on that line.

concepts.name: :vimgrep native regex engine
concepts.evidence: The :vimgrep command allows us to search through multiple files using Vim’s native regular expression engine.

concepts.name: g flag for all matches
concepts.evidence: If we supply the g flag after the pattern, then :vimgrep will match all occurrences of the specified pattern, not just the first match on each line:

concepts.name: ## argument-list expansion
concepts.evidence: As well as being able to use * and ** wildcards, we can use the ## symbol, which is expanded to represent the names of each file in the argument list (cmdline-specialⓘ).

concepts.name: empty pattern reuses current search
concepts.evidence: We can leave the pattern field empty, which tells :vimgrep to use the current search pattern.

concepts.name: search-history dependence
concepts.evidence: One thing to watch out for with this command is that it will always use the current values from the argument list and search history.
